**Rick Douglas Husband** (July 12, 1957– February 1, 2003) was an American [astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") and [fighter pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighter_pilot "Fighter pilot"). He traveled into space twice: as pilot of [STS-96](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-96 "STS-96") and commander of [STS-107](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-107 "STS-107"). Husband and the rest of the crew of STS-107 were killed when _Columbia_[disintegrated during reentry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Columbia_disaster "Space Shuttle Columbia disaster") into the [Earth's atmosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth's_atmosphere "Earth's atmosphere"). He is also a recipient of the [Congressional Space Medal of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Space_Medal_of_Honor "Congressional Space Medal of Honor").

## Early life, education and training

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rick_Husband&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life, education and training")]

Husband was born on July 12, 1957, in [Amarillo, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amarillo,_Texas "Amarillo, Texas").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-NASA_Bio-1) At age 17, he earned his pilot's license while flying out of [Tradewind Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tradewind_Airport "Tradewind Airport"). Husband graduated with honors from [Amarillo High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amarillo_High_School "Amarillo High School") in 1975.

Husband earned a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in [mechanical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanical_engineering "Mechanical engineering") from [Texas Tech University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Tech_University "Texas Tech University") in 1980 after five years of study. He earned his [Master of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science") degree from [Fresno State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresno_State_University "Fresno State University"). Upon graduation, Husband was commissioned as a pilot in the [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force"), having been enrolled in [ROTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ROTC "ROTC") his last two years of college. Husband underwent pilot training at [Vance Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vance_Air_Force_Base "Vance Air Force Base"), in [Enid, Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enid,_Oklahoma "Enid, Oklahoma"). This was followed by Land Survival School at [Fairchild Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairchild_Air_Force_Base "Fairchild Air Force Base"), in [Spokane, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spokane,_Washington "Spokane, Washington"), and [Fighter Lead-in School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trainer_aircraft#Lead-in_fighter_training "Trainer aircraft") in New Mexico. After he got married on February 27, 1982, Husband trained in the [F-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-4 "F-4") at [Homestead Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homestead_Air_Force_Base "Homestead Air Force Base") next.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-Rick-2)

## U.S. Air Force career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rick_Husband&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: U.S. Air Force career")]

Husband was assigned to a squadron at [Moody Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moody_Air_Force_Base "Moody Air Force Base") in [Valdosta, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valdosta,_Georgia "Valdosta, Georgia"), flying the F-4E. He then transferred to [George AFB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_AFB "George AFB"), in [Victorville, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorville,_California "Victorville, California") in December 1985, where Husband became an F-4 instructor. By then, he had accumulated 1000 hours of flying time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-Rick-2):30,32

In December 1987, Husband was assigned to [Edwards Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwards_Air_Force_Base "Edwards Air Force Base") in [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), where he attended the [USAF Test Pilot School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USAF_Test_Pilot_School "USAF Test Pilot School") class 88A along with future [Canadian Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Space_Agency "Canadian Space Agency") astronaut [Chris Hadfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Hadfield "Chris Hadfield"). Upon completion of test pilot school, Husband served as a test pilot flying the F-4 and all five models of the [F-15 Eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-15_Eagle "F-15 Eagle"). In the F-15 Combined Test Force, he was the program manager for the [Pratt & Whitney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pratt_&_Whitney "Pratt & Whitney")[F100-PW-229](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pratt_&_Whitney_F100#F100-PW-229 "Pratt & Whitney F100") increased performance engine and also served as the F-15 Aerial Demonstration Pilot.

In June 1992, Husband was assigned to the Aircraft and Armament Evaluation Establishment at [Boscombe Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boscombe_Down "Boscombe Down"), England, as an exchange test pilot with the [Royal Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Force "Royal Air Force"). At Boscombe Down, he was the Tornado GR1 and GR4 Project Pilot and served as a test pilot in the Hawk, Hunter, Buccaneer, Jet Provost, Tucano, and Harvard.

Husband logged over 3,800 hours of flight time in more than 40 different types of [aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft "Aircraft").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-NASA_Bio-1)

## NASA career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rick_Husband&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NASA career")]

Husband was selected as an astronaut candidate by [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") in December 1994, the same week he was promoted to lieutenant colonel.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-Rick-2):67 Husband reported to the [Johnson Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Space_Center "Johnson Space Center") in March 1995 to begin a year of training and evaluation. Upon completion of training, he was named the Astronaut Office representative for Advanced Projects at Johnson Space Center, working on [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle") Upgrades, the [Crew Return Vehicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crew_Return_Vehicle "Crew Return Vehicle") (CRV) and studies to return to the [Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon "Moon") and travel to [Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars "Mars"). Husband eventually served as Chief of Safety for the [Astronaut Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut_Office "Astronaut Office"). In 1999, he flew as pilot on [STS-96](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-96 "STS-96") and logged 235 hours and 13 minutes in [space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_space "Outer space"). Husband was later assigned to command the crew of [STS-107](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-107 "STS-107"), which was launched early in 2003. Along with the rest of the STS-107 crew, he was killed upon reentry when the shuttle disintegrated over Texas.

## Shuttle missions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rick_Husband&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Shuttle missions")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/STS-96_Rick_Husband_and_Tamara_Jernigan.jpg/250px-STS-96_Rick_Husband_and_Tamara_Jernigan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS-96_Rick_Husband_and_Tamara_Jernigan.jpg)

Pilot (PLT) Rick D. Husband (left) and EVA Specialist [Tamara E. Jernigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamara_E._Jernigan "Tamara E. Jernigan") (right) during STS-96

*   [STS-96](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-96 "STS-96") (May 27 to June 6, 1999) aboard the [Space Shuttle _Discovery_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery") was a 10-day mission during which the crew performed the first docking with the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") and delivered four tons of logistics and supplies in preparation for the arrival of the [first crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_1 "Expedition 1") to live on the station early the following year. The mission was accomplished in 153 Earth orbits, traveling 4 million miles in 9 days, 19 hours and 13 minutes.

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Commander_%28CDR%29_Rick_D._Husband_%28left%29_and_Payload_Specialist_%28PS%29_Ilan_Ramon_%28right%29_during_STS-107.jpg/250px-Commander_%28CDR%29_Rick_D._Husband_%28left%29_and_Payload_Specialist_%28PS%29_Ilan_Ramon_%28right%29_during_STS-107.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Commander_(CDR)_Rick_D._Husband_(left)_and_Payload_Specialist_(PS)_Ilan_Ramon_(right)_during_STS-107.jpg)

Commander (CDR) Rick D. Husband (left) and Payload Specialist (PS) Ilan Ramon (right) during STS-107

*   [STS-107](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-107 "STS-107") (January 16 to February 1, 2003) aboard the [Space Shuttle _Columbia_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Columbia "Space Shuttle Columbia") was a 16-day mission during which the crew performed over 80 experiments testing applications of [microgravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microgravity "Microgravity") to gain insight into the environment of space and improve life on Earth as well as enable future space exploration. The mission ended on the morning of February 1 when the shuttle disintegrated upon reentry killing all crew members, including Husband (see [Space Shuttle _Columbia_ disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Columbia_disaster "Space Shuttle Columbia disaster")).

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rick_Husband&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Rick_Husband%27s_Camaro_on_display_at_Rick_Husband_Amarillo_International_Airport.jpg/250px-Rick_Husband%27s_Camaro_on_display_at_Rick_Husband_Amarillo_International_Airport.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rick_Husband's_Camaro_on_display_at_Rick_Husband_Amarillo_International_Airport.jpg)

Husband's Camaro on display at Rick Husband Amarillo International Airport

Husband's wife, Evelyn (born September 18, 1958), details her [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") life with Rick and his struggles to fulfill his lifelong dream to become an astronaut in the 2004 book _High Calling: The Courageous Life and Faith of Space Shuttle Columbia Commander Rick Husband_ co-written with Donna VanLiere. They had two children together: Laura Marie (born October 5, 1990) and Matthew (born August 3, 1995). Evelyn married Bill Thompson in January 2008 and was the keynote speaker for the memorial ceremony at the Astronaut Memorial "Space Mirror" at the [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center") in [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida"), five years after the Space Shuttle _Columbia_ tragedy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-7)

**Rick Douglas Husband** (July 12, 1957– February 1, 2003) was an American [astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") and [fighter pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighter_pilot "Fighter pilot"). He traveled into space twice: as pilot of [STS-96](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-96 "STS-96") and commander of [STS-107](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-107 "STS-107"). Husband and the rest of the crew of STS-107 were killed when _Columbia_[disintegrated during reentry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Columbia_disaster "Space Shuttle Columbia disaster") into the [Earth's atmosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth's_atmosphere "Earth's atmosphere"). He is also a recipient of the [Congressional Space Medal of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Space_Medal_of_Honor "Congressional Space Medal of Honor").

## Early life, education and training

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rick_Husband&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life, education and training")]

Husband was born on July 12, 1957, in [Amarillo, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amarillo,_Texas "Amarillo, Texas").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-NASA_Bio-1) At age 17, he earned his pilot's license while flying out of [Tradewind Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tradewind_Airport "Tradewind Airport"). Husband graduated with honors from [Amarillo High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amarillo_High_School "Amarillo High School") in 1975.

Husband earned a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in [mechanical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanical_engineering "Mechanical engineering") from [Texas Tech University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Tech_University "Texas Tech University") in 1980 after five years of study. He earned his [Master of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science") degree from [Fresno State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresno_State_University "Fresno State University"). Upon graduation, Husband was commissioned as a pilot in the [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force"), having been enrolled in [ROTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ROTC "ROTC") his last two years of college. Husband underwent pilot training at [Vance Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vance_Air_Force_Base "Vance Air Force Base"), in [Enid, Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enid,_Oklahoma "Enid, Oklahoma"). This was followed by Land Survival School at [Fairchild Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairchild_Air_Force_Base "Fairchild Air Force Base"), in [Spokane, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spokane,_Washington "Spokane, Washington"), and [Fighter Lead-in School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trainer_aircraft#Lead-in_fighter_training "Trainer aircraft") in New Mexico. After he got married on February 27, 1982, Husband trained in the [F-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-4 "F-4") at [Homestead Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homestead_Air_Force_Base "Homestead Air Force Base") next.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-Rick-2)

## U.S. Air Force career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rick_Husband&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: U.S. Air Force career")]

Husband was assigned to a squadron at [Moody Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moody_Air_Force_Base "Moody Air Force Base") in [Valdosta, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valdosta,_Georgia "Valdosta, Georgia"), flying the F-4E. He then transferred to [George AFB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_AFB "George AFB"), in [Victorville, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorville,_California "Victorville, California") in December 1985, where Husband became an F-4 instructor. By then, he had accumulated 1000 hours of flying time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-Rick-2):30,32

In December 1987, Husband was assigned to [Edwards Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwards_Air_Force_Base "Edwards Air Force Base") in [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), where he attended the [USAF Test Pilot School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USAF_Test_Pilot_School "USAF Test Pilot School") class 88A along with future [Canadian Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Space_Agency "Canadian Space Agency") astronaut [Chris Hadfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Hadfield "Chris Hadfield"). Upon completion of test pilot school, Husband served as a test pilot flying the F-4 and all five models of the [F-15 Eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-15_Eagle "F-15 Eagle"). In the F-15 Combined Test Force, he was the program manager for the [Pratt & Whitney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pratt_&_Whitney "Pratt & Whitney")[F100-PW-229](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pratt_&_Whitney_F100#F100-PW-229 "Pratt & Whitney F100") increased performance engine and also served as the F-15 Aerial Demonstration Pilot.

In June 1992, Husband was assigned to the Aircraft and Armament Evaluation Establishment at [Boscombe Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boscombe_Down "Boscombe Down"), England, as an exchange test pilot with the [Royal Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Force "Royal Air Force"). At Boscombe Down, he was the Tornado GR1 and GR4 Project Pilot and served as a test pilot in the Hawk, Hunter, Buccaneer, Jet Provost, Tucano, and Harvard.

Husband logged over 3,800 hours of flight time in more than 40 different types of [aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft "Aircraft").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-NASA_Bio-1)

## NASA career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rick_Husband&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NASA career")]

Husband was selected as an astronaut candidate by [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") in December 1994, the same week he was promoted to lieutenant colonel.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-Rick-2):67 Husband reported to the [Johnson Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Space_Center "Johnson Space Center") in March 1995 to begin a year of training and evaluation. Upon completion of training, he was named the Astronaut Office representative for Advanced Projects at Johnson Space Center, working on [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle") Upgrades, the [Crew Return Vehicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crew_Return_Vehicle "Crew Return Vehicle") (CRV) and studies to return to the [Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon "Moon") and travel to [Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars "Mars"). Husband eventually served as Chief of Safety for the [Astronaut Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut_Office "Astronaut Office"). In 1999, he flew as pilot on [STS-96](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-96 "STS-96") and logged 235 hours and 13 minutes in [space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_space "Outer space"). Husband was later assigned to command the crew of [STS-107](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-107 "STS-107"), which was launched early in 2003. Along with the rest of the STS-107 crew, he was killed upon reentry when the shuttle disintegrated over Texas.

## Shuttle missions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rick_Husband&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Shuttle missions")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/STS-96_Rick_Husband_and_Tamara_Jernigan.jpg/250px-STS-96_Rick_Husband_and_Tamara_Jernigan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:STS-96_Rick_Husband_and_Tamara_Jernigan.jpg)

Pilot (PLT) Rick D. Husband (left) and EVA Specialist [Tamara E. Jernigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamara_E._Jernigan "Tamara E. Jernigan") (right) during STS-96

*   [STS-96](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-96 "STS-96") (May 27 to June 6, 1999) aboard the [Space Shuttle _Discovery_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery") was a 10-day mission during which the crew performed the first docking with the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") and delivered four tons of logistics and supplies in preparation for the arrival of the [first crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_1 "Expedition 1") to live on the station early the following year. The mission was accomplished in 153 Earth orbits, traveling 4 million miles in 9 days, 19 hours and 13 minutes.

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Commander_%28CDR%29_Rick_D._Husband_%28left%29_and_Payload_Specialist_%28PS%29_Ilan_Ramon_%28right%29_during_STS-107.jpg/250px-Commander_%28CDR%29_Rick_D._Husband_%28left%29_and_Payload_Specialist_%28PS%29_Ilan_Ramon_%28right%29_during_STS-107.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Commander_(CDR)_Rick_D._Husband_(left)_and_Payload_Specialist_(PS)_Ilan_Ramon_(right)_during_STS-107.jpg)

Commander (CDR) Rick D. Husband (left) and Payload Specialist (PS) Ilan Ramon (right) during STS-107

*   [STS-107](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-107 "STS-107") (January 16 to February 1, 2003) aboard the [Space Shuttle _Columbia_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Columbia "Space Shuttle Columbia") was a 16-day mission during which the crew performed over 80 experiments testing applications of [microgravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microgravity "Microgravity") to gain insight into the environment of space and improve life on Earth as well as enable future space exploration. The mission ended on the morning of February 1 when the shuttle disintegrated upon reentry killing all crew members, including Husband (see [Space Shuttle _Columbia_ disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Columbia_disaster "Space Shuttle Columbia disaster")).

*   Rick Husband Boulevard [Howardwick, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howardwick,_Texas "Howardwick, Texas").

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rick_Husband&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Rick_Husband%27s_Camaro_on_display_at_Rick_Husband_Amarillo_International_Airport.jpg/250px-Rick_Husband%27s_Camaro_on_display_at_Rick_Husband_Amarillo_International_Airport.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rick_Husband's_Camaro_on_display_at_Rick_Husband_Amarillo_International_Airport.jpg)

Husband's Camaro on display at Rick Husband Amarillo International Airport

Husband's wife, Evelyn (born September 18, 1958), details her [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") life with Rick and his struggles to fulfill his lifelong dream to become an astronaut in the 2004 book _High Calling: The Courageous Life and Faith of Space Shuttle Columbia Commander Rick Husband_ co-written with Donna VanLiere. They had two children together: Laura Marie (born October 5, 1990) and Matthew (born August 3, 1995). Evelyn married Bill Thompson in January 2008 and was the keynote speaker for the memorial ceremony at the Astronaut Memorial "Space Mirror" at the [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center") in [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida"), five years after the Space Shuttle _Columbia_ tragedy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Husband#cite_note-7)

**NASA Astronaut Group 15** ("The Flying Escargot") was a group of 23 [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") astronauts announced on December 8, 1994.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_94-205-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-ap-1994-12-09-2) Group members adopted _The Flying Escargot_ as their moniker, in reference to two members of the group being from [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-t-shirt-si-3) The group featured ten [pilots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviator "Aviator"), nine [mission specialists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_specialist "Mission specialist"), and four international mission specialist trainees from France,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_95-016-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_97-199-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_H97-263-6) Canada[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_95-003-7) and Japan.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_95-003-7)

Three members of this group, Rick Husband, [Michael P. Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_P._Anderson "Michael P. Anderson"), and [Kalpana Chawla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalpana_Chawla "Kalpana Chawla"), died in the [Space Shuttle _Columbia_ disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Columbia_disaster "Space Shuttle Columbia disaster").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_j03-07-8) These three received the [Congressional Space Medal of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Space_Medal_of_Honor "Congressional Space Medal of Honor").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-rdhusband-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-mpanderson-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-kchawla-11)

Another member of the group [Pamela Melroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy "Pamela Melroy"), served as [Deputy Administrator of NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Administrator_of_NASA "Deputy Administrator of NASA") from 2021 to 2025, having been appointed by US President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-12)

1994 human spaceflight selection of 23 candidates; "The Flying Escargot"

| The Flying Escargot |
| --- |
| [![Image 4: Official group portrait](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15.jpg/250px-NASA_Astronaut_Group_15.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NASA_Astronaut_Group_15.jpg) The astronauts of Group 15 |
| Year selected | 1994 |
| Number selected | 23 |
| ←[14 (1992)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_14 "NASA Astronaut Group 14") [16 (1996)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_16 "NASA Astronaut Group 16")→ |

**NASA Astronaut Group 15** ("The Flying Escargot") was a group of 23 [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") astronauts announced on December 8, 1994.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_94-205-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-ap-1994-12-09-2) Group members adopted _The Flying Escargot_ as their moniker, in reference to two members of the group being from [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-t-shirt-si-3) The group featured ten [pilots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviator "Aviator"), nine [mission specialists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_specialist "Mission specialist"), and four international mission specialist trainees from France,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_95-016-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_97-199-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_H97-263-6) Canada[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_95-003-7) and Japan.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_95-003-7)

Three members of this group, Rick Husband, [Michael P. Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_P._Anderson "Michael P. Anderson"), and [Kalpana Chawla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalpana_Chawla "Kalpana Chawla"), died in the [Space Shuttle _Columbia_ disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Columbia_disaster "Space Shuttle Columbia disaster").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-release_j03-07-8) These three received the [Congressional Space Medal of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Space_Medal_of_Honor "Congressional Space Medal of Honor").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-rdhusband-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-mpanderson-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-kchawla-11)

Another member of the group [Pamela Melroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy "Pamela Melroy"), served as [Deputy Administrator of NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Administrator_of_NASA "Deputy Administrator of NASA") from 2021 to 2025, having been appointed by US President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Group_15#cite_note-12)

Biographical Data

Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center
Houston, Texas  77058  National Aeronautics and
Space Administration

KALPANA CHAWLA (PH.D.)
NASA ASTRONAUT (DECEASED)

PERSONAL DATA:  Born in Karnal, India.  Died on February 1, 2003 over the southern
United States when Space Shuttle Columbia  and her crew perished during entry, 16
minutes prior to scheduled landing.  She is survived by her husband.  Kalpana Chawla
enjoyed flying, hiking, back-  packing, and reading.  She held a  Certificated Flight
Instructor's license with airplane and glider ratings, Commercial Pilot's licenses for single-
and multi-engine land and seaplanes, and Gliders, and instrument rating for airplanes.  She
enjoyed flying aerobatics and tail-  wheel airplanes.

EDUCATION:  Graduated from Tagore School, Karnal, India, in 1976.  Bachelor of
science degree in aeronautical engineering from Punjab Engineering College, India, 1982.
Master of science degree in aerospace engineering from University of Texas, 1984.
Doctorate of philosophy in aerospace engineering from University of Colorado, 1988.

AWARDS:  Posthumously awarded the Congressional Space Medal of Honor, the NASA
Space Flight Medal, and the NASA Distinguished Service Medal.

EXPERIENCE:  In 1988, Kalpana Chawla started work at NASA Ames Research Center in the area of powered  -lift computational
fluid dynamics.  Her research concentrated on simulation of complex air flows encountered around aircraft such as the Harrier  in
" ground-effect."  Following completion of this project she supported research in mapping of flow solvers to parallel computers, and
testing of these solvers by carrying out powered lift computations.  In 1993 Kalpana Chawla joined Overset Methods Inc., Los
Altos, California, as Vice President and Research Scientist to form a team with other researchers specializing in simulation of
moving multiple body problems.  She was responsible for development and implementation of efficient techniques to perform
aerodynamic optimization.  Results of various projects that Kalpana Chawla participated in are documented in technical conference
papers and journals.

NASA EXPERIENCE:  Selected by NASA in December 1994, Kalpana Chawla reported to the Johnson Space Center in March
1995 as an astronaut candidate in the 15th Group of Astronauts.  After completing a year of training and evaluation, she was
assigned as crew representative to work technical issues for the Astronaut Office EVA/Robotics and Computer Branches.  Her
assignments included work on development of Robotic Situational Awareness Displays and testing space shuttle control software in
the Shuttle Avionics Integration Laboratory.  In November, 1996, Kalpana Chawla was assigned as mission specialist and prime
robotic arm operator on ST S  -87.  In January 1998, she was assigned as crew representative for shuttle and station flight crew
equipment, and subsequently served as lead for Astronaut Office’s Crew Systems and Habitability section.  She flew on STS-87
(1997) and STS-107 (2003), logging 30 days, 14 hours and 54 minutes in space.

SPACE FLIGHT EXPERIENCE:  ST S-  87  Columbia  (November 19 to December 5, 1997).  STS-87 was the fourth U.S
Microgravity P ayload flight and focused on experiments designed to study how the weightless environment of space affects various
physical processes, and on observations of the Sun's outer atmospheric layers.  Two members of the crew performed an EVA
(spacewalk) which featured the manual capture of a Spartan satellite, in addition to testing EVA tools and procedures for future
Space Station assembly.  ST S-87 made 252 orbits of the Earth, traveling  6.5 million miles in in 376 hours and 34 minutes.

ST S-  107  Columbia  (January 16 to February 1, 2003).  T he 16  -day flight was a dedicated science and research mission.  Working
24 hours a day, in two alternating shifts, the crew successfully conducted approximately 80 experiments.  The STS-107 mission
ended abruptly on February 1, 2003 when Space Shuttle Columbia  and  the  crew perished during entry, 16 minutes prior to
scheduled landing.

**Ilan Ramon** ([Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language"): אילן רמון; pronounced[[(ʔ)iˈlan ʁaˈmon]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hebrew "Help:IPA/Hebrew"); June 20, 1954 – February 1, 2003)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-Stone20032-1) was an [Israeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel")[fighter pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighter_pilot "Fighter pilot") and later the first Israeli [astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut"). He served as a [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle") payload specialist on [STS-107](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-107 "STS-107"), the fatal mission of _[Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Columbia "Space Shuttle Columbia")_, in which he and the six other crew members were killed when the spacecraft [disintegrated during re-entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Columbia_disaster "Space Shuttle Columbia disaster"). At 48, Ramon was the oldest member of the crew. He is the first foreign recipient of the United States [Congressional Space Medal of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Space_Medal_of_Honor "Congressional Space Medal of Honor"), which was awarded posthumously.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-2)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Born as Ilan Wolfferman in [Ramat Gan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramat_Gan "Ramat Gan"), Israel, to Tonya (1929–2003) and Eliezer Wolfferman (1923–2006), a family of [Ashkenazi Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jewish "Ashkenazi Jewish") descent, Ramon grew up in [Beersheba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beersheba "Beersheba"). His father was from [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Jews "German Jews"), and his family fled [Nazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany") persecution in 1935. His mother and grandmother were from [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Jews "Polish Jews"), and were [Holocaust survivors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocaust_survivors "Holocaust survivors"), having been in [Auschwitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auschwitz "Auschwitz"). They [emigrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah "Aliyah") to Israel in 1949.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-3) Ramon's first name, Ilan, means "tree" in [Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-4) Ramon [Hebraizied his surname](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebraization_of_surnames "Hebraization of surnames") from **Wolfferman** to **Ramon**, a more "Israeli ([Sabra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabra_(person) "Sabra (person)"))" name, when he joined the [Israeli Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force "Israeli Air Force") (IAF). This was customary and expected of IAF pilots, as well as among [IDF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces "Israel Defense Forces") senior officers at the time.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-5)

Ramon graduated from high school in 1972. In 1987, he graduated with a [B.Sc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in electronics and computer engineering from [Tel Aviv University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv_University "Tel Aviv University").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-nasabio-6)

## Air Force career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Air Force career")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Colonel_ilan_ramon_%2C_israeli_air_force_website.jpg/250px-Colonel_ilan_ramon_%2C_israeli_air_force_website.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colonel_ilan_ramon_,_israeli_air_force_website.jpg)

Ramon as a Colonel in the Israeli Air Force

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/IAF_F-16A_Netz_243_CIAF_2004.jpg/250px-IAF_F-16A_Netz_243_CIAF_2004.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:IAF_F-16A_Netz_243_CIAF_2004.jpg)

The [F-16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-16 "F-16")_Netz #243_ flown by Ramon in [Operation Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Opera "Operation Opera"). The green and black triangular emblem on the nose commemorates the attack.

Ramon was a [Colonel (_Aluf Mishne_)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces_ranks "Israel Defense Forces ranks") and a [fighter pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighter_aircraft "Fighter aircraft") in the [Israeli Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force "Israeli Air Force"), with thousands of hours of [flying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight "Flight") experience. He began the fighter pilot's course at the [Israeli Air Force Flight Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force_Flight_Academy "Israeli Air Force Flight Academy") in 1972, but was forced to suspend his studies after breaking his hand. Ramon served in an [electronic warfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_warfare "Electronic warfare") unit in the [Sinai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula "Sinai Peninsula") during the [Yom Kippur War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War "Yom Kippur War"), and afterwards, returned to the flight academy. He graduated from the fighter pilots' course in 1974. From 1974 to 1976, Ramon participated in [A-4 Skyhawk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-4_Skyhawk "A-4 Skyhawk") Basic Training and Operations. From 1976 to 1980, he participated in training and operations for the [Mirage IIIC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Mirage_III "Dassault Mirage III"). In 1980, as one of the IAF's establishment team of the first F-16 Squadron in Israel, Ramon attended the F-16 Training Course at [Hill Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hill_Air_Force_Base "Hill Air Force Base"), [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah"). From 1981 to 1983, he served as the Deputy Squadron Commander B, F-16 Squadron.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-nasabio-6)

In 1981, Ramon was the youngest pilot taking part in [Operation Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Opera "Operation Opera"), Israel's strike against [Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq "Iraq")'s unfinished [Osiraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osirak "Osirak")[nuclear reactor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_reactor "Nuclear reactor"). The facility was destroyed, killing ten Iraqi soldiers and one French researcher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-8) Ramon also flew in the [1982 Lebanon War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Lebanon_War "1982 Lebanon War").

After attending [Tel Aviv University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv_University "Tel Aviv University"), Ramon served as Deputy Squadron Commander A, [119 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/119_Squadron_(Israel) "119 Squadron (Israel)"), flying the [F-4 Phantom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-4_Phantom "F-4 Phantom") (1988–1990). In 1990, he attended the Squadron Commanders Course and between 1990 and 1992, commanded [117 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/117_Squadron_(Israel) "117 Squadron (Israel)"), flying the [F-16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-16_Fighting_Falcon "F-16 Fighting Falcon"). From 1992 to 1994, Ramon was head of the Aircraft Branch in the Operations Requirement Department. In 1994, he was promoted to the rank of colonel and assigned as head of the Department of Operational Requirement for Weapon Development and Acquisition. Ramon stayed at this post until 1998.

Ramon accumulated over 3,000 flight hours on the A-4, Mirage IIIC, and F-4, and over 1,000 flight hours on the F-16.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-nasabio-6)

## NASA experience

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NASA experience")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Ilan_Ramon.jpg/250px-Ilan_Ramon.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ilan_Ramon.jpg)

Ramon in November 2001

### NASA on-ground trainings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: NASA on-ground trainings")]

In 1997, Ramon was selected as a [Payload Specialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payload_Specialist "Payload Specialist"). He was designated to train as prime for a space shuttle mission with a payload that included a [multispectral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multispectral "Multispectral") camera for recording desert [aerosol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerosol "Aerosol") (dust). In July 1998, Ramon reported for training at the [Johnson Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Space_Center "Johnson Space Center") in [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"), Texas, where he trained until 2003. Ramon flew aboard [STS-107](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-107 "STS-107"), logging 15 days, 22 hours and 20 minutes in space.

### Space flight: STS-107, Space Shuttle _Columbia_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Space flight: STS-107, Space Shuttle Columbia")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Ilan_ramon_sts-107.jpg/250px-Ilan_ramon_sts-107.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ilan_ramon_sts-107.jpg)

Ramon photographed aboard _Columbia_ on January 26, 2003

STS-107 _Columbia_ (January 16 – February 1, 2003), a 16-day flight, was a dedicated science and research mission. Working 24 hours a day, in two alternating shifts, the crew successfully conducted approximately 80 experiments.

Personally nonreligious, Ramon performed traditional observance while in orbit: "I feel I am representing all Jews and all Israelis." He was the first astronaut to request [kosher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosher "Kosher") food and marked the Sabbath.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-9) Ramon, whose mother and grandmother were survivors of [Auschwitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auschwitz "Auschwitz"), was asked by S. Isaac Mekel, director of development at the American Society for [Yad Vashem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yad_Vashem "Yad Vashem"), to take an item from Yad Vashem aboard STS-107. Ramon carried with him a pencil sketch, _Moon Landscape_, drawn by 16-year-old [Petr Ginz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petr_Ginz "Petr Ginz"), who was murdered in Auschwitz. Ramon also took with him a [microfiche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microfiche "Microfiche") copy of the [Torah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torah "Torah") given to him by Israeli president [Moshe Katsav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moshe_Katsav "Moshe Katsav") and a miniature Torah scroll (from the Holocaust) that was given to him by Prof. Yehoyachin Yosef, a [Bergen Belsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bergen_Belsen "Bergen Belsen") survivor.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-10) Ramon asked the 1939 Club, a [Holocaust survivor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocaust_survivor "Holocaust survivor") organization in Los Angeles, for a symbol of the Holocaust to take into outer space with him. A barbed wire [mezuzah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mezuzah "Mezuzah") by the [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") artist [Aimee Golant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aimee_Golant?action=edit&redlink=1 "Aimee Golant (page does not exist)") was selected. Ramon also took with him a dollar of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi [Menachem M. Schneerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menachem_M._Schneerson "Menachem M. Schneerson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-11)

Ramon and the rest of the _Columbia_ crew died over East Texas in the [Southern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States "Southern United States") during entry into Earth's atmosphere, 16 minutes before scheduled landing.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-nasabio-6)

### Diary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Diary")]

Among the recovered 40% from the contents of the _Columbia_ Space Shuttle that broke up over Texas were 37 pages of Ramon's diary, which NASA returned to his wife.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-PC40.Wired-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-13) His widow, Rona,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-PC40.Wired-12) shared an excerpt with the Israeli public in a display at [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem")'s [Israel Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Museum "Israel Museum").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-diary1-14) Rona Ramon brought it to Israel Museum [forensic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forensic "Forensic") experts. Only two pages were displayed, one containing Ramon's notes, and the other is a copy of the [Kiddush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiddush "Kiddush")[prayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prayer "Prayer").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-diary1-14)[Curator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curator "Curator")[Yigal Zalmona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yigal_Zalmona "Yigal Zalmona")[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-15) said the [diary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diary "Diary") was partially restored in one year, and needed four more, for police scientists to decipher 80% of the text. Zalmona stated: "The diary survived extreme heat in the explosion, extreme atmospheric cold, and then was attacked by microorganisms and insects. It's almost a miracle that it survived — it's incredible. There is 'no rational explanation' for how it was recovered when most of the shuttle was not."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-diary1-14) Ramon wrote on the last day of the journal:

> Today was the first day that I felt that I am truly living in space. I have become a man who lives and works in space.

Inscribed in black ink and [pencil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pencil "Pencil"), it covered the first six days of the 16-day mission.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-16)

## Family

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Family")]

Ramon was survived by his wife, Rona, and their four children: Assaf, Tal, Yiftah, and Noa, who were in Florida at the time of the accident. Ramon's widow, [Rona Ramon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rona_Ramon "Rona Ramon"), served in the Israel Defense Forces as a paramedic and later earned a BA at the [Wingate Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wingate_Institute "Wingate Institute"). After Assaf's death, she returned to university and graduated with a master's degree in holistic health at [Lesley University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesley_University "Lesley University"), Massachusetts. She also lectured about dealing with grief and finding coping mechanisms. Rona served as founding CEO of the nonprofit Ramon Foundation for youth academic excellence and social leadership through science and technology.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-17) She died of pancreatic cancer on December 17, 2018.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-18) She was posthumously awarded the [Israel Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Prize "Israel Prize") for lifetime achievement.

Ramon's eldest son, Assaf (February 10, 1988 – September 13, 2009), died at age 21 during a routine training flight while piloting his [F-16A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Dynamics_F-16_Fighting_Falcon "General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon"), three months after graduating from the [IAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force "Israeli Air Force") flight school [Hatzerim Airbase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatzerim_Airbase "Hatzerim Airbase") as the top cadet in his class.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-22) Assaf lost consciousness during a spell of vertigo, as a result of the high speed and G-force conditions to which he was subjected. This led to the plane crash and Assaf's subsequent death. He was considered an excellent pilot.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-Boudreaux-23) A lieutenant of the [Israeli Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force "Israeli Air Force"), he was posthumously promoted to the rank of captain.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-Boudreaux-23)

On November 10, 2013, the American Society for Yad Vashem held a special event with the participation of Ramon's son, Tal, who performed a song he wrote in memory of his father.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-JPost_2016-24) Tal Ramon performed his debut album, _Dmut_, at the club Zappa Tel Aviv in 2016.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-JPost_2016-24)

**Ilan Ramon** ([Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language"): אילן רמון; pronounced[[(ʔ)iˈlan ʁaˈmon]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hebrew "Help:IPA/Hebrew"); June 20, 1954 – February 1, 2003)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-Stone20032-1) was an [Israeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel")[fighter pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighter_pilot "Fighter pilot") and later the first Israeli [astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut"). He served as a [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle") payload specialist on [STS-107](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-107 "STS-107"), the fatal mission of _[Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Columbia "Space Shuttle Columbia")_, in which he and the six other crew members were killed when the spacecraft [disintegrated during re-entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Columbia_disaster "Space Shuttle Columbia disaster"). At 48, Ramon was the oldest member of the crew. He is the first foreign recipient of the United States [Congressional Space Medal of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Space_Medal_of_Honor "Congressional Space Medal of Honor"), which was awarded posthumously.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-2)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Born as Ilan Wolfferman in [Ramat Gan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramat_Gan "Ramat Gan"), Israel, to Tonya (1929–2003) and Eliezer Wolfferman (1923–2006), a family of [Ashkenazi Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jewish "Ashkenazi Jewish") descent, Ramon grew up in [Beersheba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beersheba "Beersheba"). His father was from [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Jews "German Jews"), and his family fled [Nazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany") persecution in 1935. His mother and grandmother were from [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Jews "Polish Jews"), and were [Holocaust survivors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocaust_survivors "Holocaust survivors"), having been in [Auschwitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auschwitz "Auschwitz"). They [emigrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah "Aliyah") to Israel in 1949.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-3) Ramon's first name, Ilan, means "tree" in [Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-4) Ramon [Hebraizied his surname](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebraization_of_surnames "Hebraization of surnames") from **Wolfferman** to **Ramon**, a more "Israeli ([Sabra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabra_(person) "Sabra (person)"))" name, when he joined the [Israeli Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force "Israeli Air Force") (IAF). This was customary and expected of IAF pilots, as well as among [IDF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces "Israel Defense Forces") senior officers at the time.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-5)

Ramon graduated from high school in 1972. In 1987, he graduated with a [B.Sc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in electronics and computer engineering from [Tel Aviv University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv_University "Tel Aviv University").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-nasabio-6)

## Air Force career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Air Force career")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Colonel_ilan_ramon_%2C_israeli_air_force_website.jpg/250px-Colonel_ilan_ramon_%2C_israeli_air_force_website.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colonel_ilan_ramon_,_israeli_air_force_website.jpg)

Ramon as a Colonel in the Israeli Air Force

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/IAF_F-16A_Netz_243_CIAF_2004.jpg/250px-IAF_F-16A_Netz_243_CIAF_2004.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:IAF_F-16A_Netz_243_CIAF_2004.jpg)

The [F-16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-16 "F-16")_Netz #243_ flown by Ramon in [Operation Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Opera "Operation Opera"). The green and black triangular emblem on the nose commemorates the attack.

Ramon was a [Colonel (_Aluf Mishne_)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces_ranks "Israel Defense Forces ranks") and a [fighter pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighter_aircraft "Fighter aircraft") in the [Israeli Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force "Israeli Air Force"), with thousands of hours of [flying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight "Flight") experience. He began the fighter pilot's course at the [Israeli Air Force Flight Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force_Flight_Academy "Israeli Air Force Flight Academy") in 1972, but was forced to suspend his studies after breaking his hand. Ramon served in an [electronic warfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_warfare "Electronic warfare") unit in the [Sinai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula "Sinai Peninsula") during the [Yom Kippur War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War "Yom Kippur War"), and afterwards, returned to the flight academy. He graduated from the fighter pilots' course in 1974. From 1974 to 1976, Ramon participated in [A-4 Skyhawk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-4_Skyhawk "A-4 Skyhawk") Basic Training and Operations. From 1976 to 1980, he participated in training and operations for the [Mirage IIIC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Mirage_III "Dassault Mirage III"). In 1980, as one of the IAF's establishment team of the first F-16 Squadron in Israel, Ramon attended the F-16 Training Course at [Hill Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hill_Air_Force_Base "Hill Air Force Base"), [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah"). From 1981 to 1983, he served as the Deputy Squadron Commander B, F-16 Squadron.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-nasabio-6)

In 1981, Ramon was the youngest pilot taking part in [Operation Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Opera "Operation Opera"), Israel's strike against [Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq "Iraq")'s unfinished [Osiraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osirak "Osirak")[nuclear reactor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_reactor "Nuclear reactor"). The facility was destroyed, killing ten Iraqi soldiers and one French researcher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-8) Ramon also flew in the [1982 Lebanon War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Lebanon_War "1982 Lebanon War").

After attending [Tel Aviv University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv_University "Tel Aviv University"), Ramon served as Deputy Squadron Commander A, [119 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/119_Squadron_(Israel) "119 Squadron (Israel)"), flying the [F-4 Phantom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-4_Phantom "F-4 Phantom") (1988–1990). In 1990, he attended the Squadron Commanders Course and between 1990 and 1992, commanded [117 Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/117_Squadron_(Israel) "117 Squadron (Israel)"), flying the [F-16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-16_Fighting_Falcon "F-16 Fighting Falcon"). From 1992 to 1994, Ramon was head of the Aircraft Branch in the Operations Requirement Department. In 1994, he was promoted to the rank of colonel and assigned as head of the Department of Operational Requirement for Weapon Development and Acquisition. Ramon stayed at this post until 1998.

Ramon accumulated over 3,000 flight hours on the A-4, Mirage IIIC, and F-4, and over 1,000 flight hours on the F-16.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-nasabio-6)

## NASA experience

Ramon in November 2001

### NASA on-ground trainings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: NASA on-ground trainings")]

In 1997, Ramon was selected as a [Payload Specialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payload_Specialist "Payload Specialist"). He was designated to train as prime for a space shuttle mission with a payload that included a [multispectral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multispectral "Multispectral") camera for recording desert [aerosol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerosol "Aerosol") (dust). In July 1998, Ramon reported for training at the [Johnson Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Space_Center "Johnson Space Center") in [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"), Texas, where he trained until 2003. Ramon flew aboard [STS-107](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-107 "STS-107"), logging 15 days, 22 hours and 20 minutes in space.

### Space flight: STS-107, Space Shuttle _Columbia_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Space flight: STS-107, Space Shuttle Columbia")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Ilan_ramon_sts-107.jpg/250px-Ilan_ramon_sts-107.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ilan_ramon_sts-107.jpg)

Ramon photographed aboard _Columbia_ on January 26, 2003

STS-107 _Columbia_ (January 16 – February 1, 2003), a 16-day flight, was a dedicated science and research mission. Working 24 hours a day, in two alternating shifts, the crew successfully conducted approximately 80 experiments.

Personally nonreligious, Ramon performed traditional observance while in orbit: "I feel I am representing all Jews and all Israelis." He was the first astronaut to request [kosher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosher "Kosher") food and marked the Sabbath.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-9) Ramon, whose mother and grandmother were survivors of [Auschwitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auschwitz "Auschwitz"), was asked by S. Isaac Mekel, director of development at the American Society for [Yad Vashem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yad_Vashem "Yad Vashem"), to take an item from Yad Vashem aboard STS-107. Ramon carried with him a pencil sketch, _Moon Landscape_, drawn by 16-year-old [Petr Ginz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petr_Ginz "Petr Ginz"), who was murdered in Auschwitz. Ramon also took with him a [microfiche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microfiche "Microfiche") copy of the [Torah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torah "Torah") given to him by Israeli president [Moshe Katsav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moshe_Katsav "Moshe Katsav") and a miniature Torah scroll (from the Holocaust) that was given to him by Prof. Yehoyachin Yosef, a [Bergen Belsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bergen_Belsen "Bergen Belsen") survivor.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-10) Ramon asked the 1939 Club, a [Holocaust survivor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocaust_survivor "Holocaust survivor") organization in Los Angeles, for a symbol of the Holocaust to take into outer space with him. A barbed wire [mezuzah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mezuzah "Mezuzah") by the [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") artist [Aimee Golant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aimee_Golant?action=edit&redlink=1 "Aimee Golant (page does not exist)") was selected. Ramon also took with him a dollar of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi [Menachem M. Schneerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menachem_M._Schneerson "Menachem M. Schneerson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-11)

Ramon and the rest of the _Columbia_ crew died over East Texas in the [Southern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States "Southern United States") during entry into Earth's atmosphere, 16 minutes before scheduled landing.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-nasabio-6)

### Diary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Diary")]

Among the recovered 40% from the contents of the _Columbia_ Space Shuttle that broke up over Texas were 37 pages of Ramon's diary, which NASA returned to his wife.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-PC40.Wired-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-13) His widow, Rona,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-PC40.Wired-12) shared an excerpt with the Israeli public in a display at [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem")'s [Israel Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Museum "Israel Museum").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-diary1-14) Rona Ramon brought it to Israel Museum [forensic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forensic "Forensic") experts. Only two pages were displayed, one containing Ramon's notes, and the other is a copy of the [Kiddush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiddush "Kiddush")[prayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prayer "Prayer").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-diary1-14)[Curator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curator "Curator")[Yigal Zalmona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yigal_Zalmona "Yigal Zalmona")[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-15) said the [diary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diary "Diary") was partially restored in one year, and needed four more, for police scientists to decipher 80% of the text. Zalmona stated: "The diary survived extreme heat in the explosion, extreme atmospheric cold, and then was attacked by microorganisms and insects. It's almost a miracle that it survived — it's incredible. There is 'no rational explanation' for how it was recovered when most of the shuttle was not."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-diary1-14) Ramon wrote on the last day of the journal:

> Today was the first day that I felt that I am truly living in space. I have become a man who lives and works in space.

Inscribed in black ink and [pencil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pencil "Pencil"), it covered the first six days of the 16-day mission.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-16)

## Family

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ilan_Ramon&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Family")]

Ramon was survived by his wife, Rona, and their four children: Assaf, Tal, Yiftah, and Noa, who were in Florida at the time of the accident. Ramon's widow, [Rona Ramon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rona_Ramon "Rona Ramon"), served in the Israel Defense Forces as a paramedic and later earned a BA at the [Wingate Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wingate_Institute "Wingate Institute"). After Assaf's death, she returned to university and graduated with a master's degree in holistic health at [Lesley University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesley_University "Lesley University"), Massachusetts. She also lectured about dealing with grief and finding coping mechanisms. Rona served as founding CEO of the nonprofit Ramon Foundation for youth academic excellence and social leadership through science and technology.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-17) She died of pancreatic cancer on December 17, 2018.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-18) She was posthumously awarded the [Israel Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Prize "Israel Prize") for lifetime achievement.

Ramon's eldest son, Assaf (February 10, 1988 – September 13, 2009), died at age 21 during a routine training flight while piloting his [F-16A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Dynamics_F-16_Fighting_Falcon "General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon"), three months after graduating from the [IAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force "Israeli Air Force") flight school [Hatzerim Airbase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatzerim_Airbase "Hatzerim Airbase") as the top cadet in his class.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-22) Assaf lost consciousness during a spell of vertigo, as a result of the high speed and G-force conditions to which he was subjected. This led to the plane crash and Assaf's subsequent death. He was considered an excellent pilot.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-Boudreaux-23) A lieutenant of the [Israeli Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Air_Force "Israeli Air Force"), he was posthumously promoted to the rank of captain.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-Boudreaux-23)

On November 10, 2013, the American Society for Yad Vashem held a special event with the participation of Ramon's son, Tal, who performed a song he wrote in memory of his father.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-JPost_2016-24) Tal Ramon performed his debut album, _Dmut_, at the club Zappa Tel Aviv in 2016.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Ramon#cite_note-JPost_2016-24)
